text: dsh-emergency-plan 是一个 DSH 工具插件，用于核对生产安全事故应急预案的章节要素并定位条款差异。它注册 emergency_plan 工具，接收 JSON、YAML 或可粘贴的章节文本，也可读取用户指定的材料文件；随后按预案类型检查章节是否齐备、是否有正文、顺序和定位信息，并核对版本记录、重复标题及可选附件项。结果按规则严重程度列出发现、引用依据、位置和未执行项，便于人工复核。适合需要快速整理预案差异的 DSH 用户。插件不需要 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-emergency-plan checks emergency plan sections in DSH. Its emergency_plan tool reads JSON, YAML, pasted text, or a selected file, then reports missing or duplicate sections, ordering and location differences, cited rule bases, and skipped checks for human review. No API key is needed.
帮我看看这份应急预案缺了哪些章节要素。
想检查预案章节顺序和页码定位有没有问题。
让 DSH 帮我找出应急预案里重复的章节标题。
预案的类型和修订版本记录是否齐全，能自动核对吗？
Can I compare an emergency plan's section headings with the expected elements and see where gaps are?
I need a report that shows which plan checks were skipped as well as the findings.
dsh-emergency-plan 的功能「预案章节要素核对」：按专项、综合或现场处置方案的规则清单查找章节，指出缺失要素或只有标题没有正文的项目，并给出章节定位。通过 emergency_plan 工具提交材料。
dsh-emergency-plan 的功能「结构差异报告」：检查章节顺序、位置、重复标题、预案类型与版本记录，并按规则输出差异、引用条款和无法执行的检查项，方便人工复核。输入支持文件或内联材料。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 它是什么：`dsh-emergency-plan` 读取一份应急预案——章节树、标题、页码与正文——按材料声明的预案类型（综合应急预案 / 专项应急预案 / 现场处置方案）套用版本化规则库，核对这份预案的要素齐备性：哪些要素已出现、哪些缺失、哪些只有标题而标题之下没有正文，以及各要素在材料里的位置——材料带页码时按页定位，否则按行号定位。每条差异都写出所依据的条款，并标明该条款是直接规定、原则性推论还是本机构配置；无法执行的检查会在 `skipped` 中说明，而不是静默通过。它只列材料与所引条款之间的字面差异，不判断内容写得好不好，也不作出合规、责任或安全定性。纯本地运行：不联网、不调用模型、不改原件。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 核心能力：- **按类型核对要素清单** —— `EP-001` 专项应急预案 7.1~7.4，`EP-002` 综合应急预案 6.1~6.5，`EP-003` 现场处置方案 8.1~8.4。标题在但标题之下没有正文的，也按“空”报出。
- **按页/行定位每条差异** —— 材料带 `page` 时按页，否则按 `line`；两者都没有时用标题定位。`EP-006` 在带页码的章节占比低于阈值时提示定位信息不足。
- **规则库是数据** —— 要素清单、别名与阈值都在 `rules/emergency-plan.yaml`。换一份 YAML 就能切换导则版本或本机构模板，不必改代码。
- **引文可核验** —— 每条规则都带文件、文号、条款号、逐字摘录、依据类型与来源地址；摘录不足八个字符、或把原则性检查标成 `error`，都会在加载期失败。
- **不静默通过** —— 未配置的要素清单、未启用的附件检查、无法排序的 `EP-005` 都会进 `skipped`。报告只列差异，措辞守卫拦截“合规/违法”一类定性词。
- **附件与版本标识按需开启** —— `EP-009` 默认关闭（`requireAttachments: false`）；`EP-008` 只有配置了 `versionPatterns` 才执行。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 规则一览：| 规则 | 检查内容 | 级别 | 依据类型 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EP-001` | 专项应急预案包含 7.1~7.4 要素 | warn | 直接规定 |
| `EP-002` | 综合应急预案包含 6.1~6.5 要素 | warn | 直接规定 |
| `EP-003` | 现场处置方案包含 8.1~8.4 要素 | warn | 直接规定 |
| `EP-004` | 材料声明三类预案中的哪一类 | warn | 直接规定 |
| `EP-005` | 要素按导则清单的顺序出现 | info | 原则性推论 |
| `EP-006` | 章节带页码，便于定位差异 | info | 原则性推论 |
| `EP-007` | 同一要素标题不重复出现 | warn | 原则性推论 |
| `EP-008` | 版本或修订标识存在（按配置） | info | 本机构配置 |
| `EP-009` | 预案带规定的附件信息（默认关闭） | info | 直接规定 |
dsh-emergency-plan README · 规则一览：要素清单在规则库而不在代码里，因为清单随导则版本变化。级别反映 GB/T 29639 是**推荐性**国家标准：要素不齐是 `warn`，不是 `error`。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 按规则的详细回答：| 你会问 | 它怎么答 |
|---|---|
| 材料里没写这是三类预案中的哪一类，会怎么样？ | `EP-004` 会报出材料未声明 `planType`，因为三类预案的要素清单各不相同。它只核对是否声明，不判断该声明是否正确；声明缺失期间，`EP-002` 与 `EP-003` 会在 `skipped` 中写明自己假定按哪一份要素清单检查。 |
| 一份综合应急预案没有「后期处置」一章，会被报出吗？还需要写「编制目的」吗？ | `EP-002` 按现行导则第 6 章的五个一级要素（6.1~6.5）逐项查找，找不到「后期处置」就报出该缺项。「编制目的」不是这五个要素之一：现行版本已将其去掉，规则库只在「总则」的别名里兼容它。该条报出的是 `warn`，因为编制导则是推荐性国家标准，不是强制要求。 |
| 专项应急预案和现场处置方案分别必须有哪些要素？ | `EP-001` 要求专项应急预案具备 7.1~7.4 要素，`EP-003` 要求现场处置方案具备 8.1~8.4 要素，各自报出在章节树里找不到的要素；标题在、标题之下没有正文的，按「空」报出。两份清单都是下限而非封闭清单——现场处置那一条的原文写着「包括但不限于」——多写要素不会被报出。7.5 应急保障在 `EP-001` 中仍属推荐项；《生产安全事故应急预案管理办法》里较短的那份清单在 `EP-003` 中单独标注为依据，不与导则的清单合并表述。 |
| 合并两份预案后，同一个要素标题出现了两次，会被查出来吗？ | `EP-007` 会报出出现不止一次的必备要素，并列出匹配到它的各个标题。这件事没有明文条款可援引——规则库依据的是目次次序的唯一性，因而封顶 `warn`——且规则库要求人工确认，因为重复通常来自合并多份预案。它比对的只是它所适用的那份要素清单，不是材料里所有重复的标题。 |
| 报告里 `EP-005` 显示 `skipped`，为什么？预案一定要标页码吗？ | `EP-005` 只有在至少两个要素带 `page` 或 `line` 时才能核对顺序，否则在 `skipped` 中说明原因，而不是凭空假定一个顺序。`EP-006` 把页码当作辅助定位信息：带页码的章节占比达到 `minPageRatio`（默认 0.5）时它不报差异，低于该比例时只作 `info` 级提示。两条都封顶 `info`——顺序要求由资料性附录推论而来，标准正文并无此规定——没有页码时也不会被表述为「不符合某条规定」，报告改按行号定位。 |
| 为什么 `EP-008` 和 `EP-009` 出现在 `skipped` 里，而不是通过？ | 两条都在等配置。`EP-009` 只有把 `requireAttachments` 设为

dsh-emergency-plan README · 依据的标准：| 文件 | 文号 | 引用它的规则 |
|---|---|---|
| 《生产经营单位生产安全事故应急预案编制导则》 | GB/T 29639-2020 | EP-001, EP-002, EP-003, EP-004, EP-005, EP-006, EP-007, EP-008, EP-009 |
| 《生产安全事故应急预案管理办法》 | 国家安全生产监督管理总局令第88号（应急管理部令第2号修正） | EP-001, EP-002, EP-003, EP-009 |

**边界**：本插件依据编制导则核对**应急预案的要素齐备性**，并按页定位每个要素，报出与所引条款之间的字面差异。它不是 `dsh-rulefile-check`（后者审查规范性文件的合法性），也不是 `dsh-hidden-risk-map`（后者把隐患台账映射到判定条款）。它读取一份预案，报出哪些要素存在、缺失或为空，以及它们位于何处。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 依据的标准：> ### ⚠️ 本插件建立在两处更正之上——请阅读
>
> **1. “八要素”不是现行要求。** 那份熟悉的清单——总则、事故风险描述、应急组织机构及职责、
> 预警及信息报告、应急响应、信息公开、后期处置、保障措施、应急预案管理——属于
> **GB/T 29639—2013**，而该标准已被**完全替代**。这一名称在任何现行国家文件中都找不到。现行标准
> **GB/T 29639-2020** 在第 6 条中为综合预案规定了**五个**一级要素（6.1 总则 / 6.2 应急组织机构及职责 /
> 6.3 应急响应 / 6.4 后期处置 / 6.5 应急保障），其前言记载**编制目的已被删除**。任何援引 2013 版条号的
> 规则都是在援引一项已废止的标准。本规则包只援引 2020 版的条号，并有测试断言 2013 版编号从不出现。
>
> **2. 页码没有强制性依据。** 没有任何国家文件要求预案标注页码；规范目次的附录是一份**资料性附录**
> （informative，非规范性），其中不含“页码”一词。因此，页码被视为**有助于评审者定位的信息**，
> 以 `info` 级别报告，且从不用“不符合 X”的措辞。当预案未标注页码时，报告回退到行号。
dsh-emergency-plan README · 依据的标准：规则库还记录了第三处较小的更正：《生产安全事故应急预案管理办法》的准确版本是**国家安全生产监督管理总局令第88号（2016），根据应急管理部令第2号（2019）修正**——不是裸的“应急管理部令第2号”——且国办发〔2013〕101号已由国办发〔2024〕5号替代。

规则级参数在 `rules/emergency-plan.yaml` 里：

dsh-emergency-plan README · 配置：- `EP-001` / `EP-002` / `EP-003` 的 `elements` —— 每种预案类型的要素清单，写成 `[{ name, aliases }]`。换导则版本或本机构模板就改这里；空列表会让该条规则报告“未配置”并进 `skipped`。
- `EP-006` 的 `minPageRatio` —— 带页码章节占比达到该值即不报差异，默认 `0.5`。
- `EP-008` 的 `versionPatterns` —— 算作版本标识的字符串；留空表示本条不执行。
- `EP-009` 的 `requireAttachments` —— 默认 `false`，因为调用方通常只给正文；只有附件真的在材料里时才设为 `true`。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 材料格式：工具接受 JSON 或 YAML，也接受纯文本预案。推荐使用章节树形式，因为抽取预案的调用方已经知道每个标题的位置：

```yaml
name: 某公司生产安全事故综合应急预案
planType: comprehensive         # comprehensive | special | on-site
sections:
  - { title: 总则, page: 1, body: 本预案适用于…… }

标题按每个要素的别名分三步放宽匹配：归一化后完全相等，其次包含，最后是较小的编辑距离，因此 `五、保障措施` 与 `二、组织机构与职责` 都能归到对应要素。比较前会剥掉编号前缀（`一、`、`1.1`、`**…**`）。直接粘贴 Markdown（`# 总则`）也能用，会按标题切分，但没有页码——报告会说明这一点。纯文本大纲也可以：每行一个短标题。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 规则来源：规则数据在 `rules/emergency-plan.yaml`。每条规则都带文件、文号、按来源自身编号体系的条款号、逐字摘录与来源地址。加载器强制：摘录必须是真实引文且不少于八个字符；只依据一般原则或本机构配置的检查，永远不得标为 `error`。

所引条款来自 **GB/T 29639-2020** 的 5.1、6、7、8、附录 C.1 与 C.3，以及 **国家安全生产监督管理总局令第88号（应急管理部令第2号修正）** 第十三、十四、十五、十六条。

有三项发现塑造了这个规则包，并记录在它的文件头里：

dsh-emergency-plan README · 规则来源：1. **“八要素”来自已废止的标准。** 现行综合预案清单是五个一级要素，且「编制目的」已被删除。
2. **页码没有强制性依据**，所以它只是 `info` 级的定位辅助，从不表述为不符合。
3. **标准代号前缀变了。** 应急管理部公告 2025 年第 1 号把 AQ/T 9011-2019 等十一项标准移到 **YJ** 前缀，顺序号、年代号与内容不变——所以配套评估导则现在写作 **YJ/T 9011-2019（原 AQ/T 9011-2019）**。评估导则与编制导则是两份文件：GB/T 29639 管**编制**，YJ/T 9011 管**评估**。

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：<details>
<summary>材料里的数据会去哪？插件联网吗？</summary>

不联网、不调用模型、不写文件。材料只从 `file` 或内联 `material` 读入，检查在纯函数里完成，结果作为工具返回值交给宿主；插件本身不落盘、不上传。宿主如何记录工具输出由宿主决定。

</details>

<details>
<summary>报告没有问题是“合规”吗？</summary>

不是。空的问题列表只说明本次执行的规则没发现差异；`skipped` 里列出的每一条都写明了没执行的原因。所有规则封顶 `warn` / `info`，报告带免责声明，措辞守卫禁止“合规 / 违法 / 责任”一类定性。

</details>

<details>
<summary>预案不标页码行不行？</summary>

没有国家文件要求预案标页码。`EP-006` 只把页码当定位辅助：带页码章节占比达到 `minPageRatio` 时不报；低于时只给 `info`。没有页码时报告按行号定位，从不表述为“不符合某条”。

</details>

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：<details>
<summary>会和别的插件抢名字吗？</summary>

只注册 `emergency_plan` 一个工具，不注册命令、服务键、客户端 slot 或 `webServer` 前缀，不监听共享事件，bundle patch 只 `insert` 自己一行。逐条说明见“与其他 DSH 插件的互操作性”。

</details>

<details>
<summary>一次检查要多久？</summary>

纯函数、单遍遍历章节树；规则库 9 条规则，无网络、无模型调用。耗时主要取决于材料大小与章节数；仓库里没有可公开的基准数据，所以这里不给出数字。

</details>

dsh-emergency-plan README · 排障：- **每个要素检查都显示为 `skipped`。** 该预案类型的 `elements` 清单为空，或材料没有声明 `planType`、检查拒绝擅自假定一种。
- **明明存在的标题被报成缺失。** 把它补进该要素的 `aliases`。匹配是字面的（上述三步放宽），不是语义识别，这是有意设计。
- **`EP-005` 不报顺序问题。** 章节既没有 `page` 也没有 `line`，没有可排序的依据，规则会在 `skipped` 里说明。
- **`EP-006` 对没有页码的预案提意见。** 这正是该规则的作用，且它是 `info`：它在告诉你报告只能引用行号。调低 `minPageRatio` 或忽略即可。
- **插件装上了但工具不出现。** 确认 `main` 指向 `lib/index.mjs` 且 `pnpm run build` 已生成该文件；`main` 写错会让加载器静默跳过该条目。
- **`dsh plugin add` 报版本不兼容。** 对等范围覆盖 `0.1.x` 与 `0.2.x`；若运行时在其之外，可显式豁免：`dsh plugin --profile <name> allow-version dsh-emergency-plan@0.1.0 --dsh-version <runtime> --accept-risk`。
- **`check` 报 `manifest-peers` 失败。** 静态检查器比对的是一份早于 0.2 世代的硬编码对等范围；安装期的对等校验以运行时为准，声明的范围才是正确的。这是 `dsh-plugin-dev` 的已知上游问题。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 安全边界与已知限制：- **只读且本地。** 插件读取 `file` 或内联 `material`，不写回、不联网、不调用模型；`package.json` 的 demo 声明 `network: false`、`writes: []`。
- **不做定性结论。** 只列材料与所引条款之间的字面差异；是否合规、是否追责、内容写得好不好，留给审核人。渲染层有措辞守卫，并始终带免责声明。
- **严重级受依据约束。** `derived-from-principle` 封顶 `warn`，`institutional-configuration` 封顶 `info`；把原则性检查标成 `error` 的规则库会在加载期失败。
- **空结果不等于通过。** 未配置的要素清单、未启用的附件检查、无法排序的条目都进 `skipped`。
- **页码不是强制要求。** 见 FAQ 与“依据的标准”第 2 条；`EP-006` 只作 `info` 提示。
- **匹配是字面的，不是语义的。** 标题按别名做归一化相等、包含与编辑距离三步匹配；同义改写需补进该要素的 `aliases`。它不判断要素正文写得对不对。
- **`planType` 未声明或无法识别。** `EP-004` 报出未声明；`EP-002` / `EP-003` 会在 `skipped` 里写明按哪份清单检查；无法识别的值会带一条警告。
- **附件与版本标识默认不查。** `EP-009` 默认 `false`；`EP-008` 的 `versionPatterns` 默认空。两者未配置时都在 `skipped` 说明。
- **规则库替换有边界。** 换成别的版本或本机构模板时，引文核验仍只对照随包的 `rules/evidence/`；新引文需要自行补核验记录。

dsh-emergency-plan README · 与其他 DSH 插件的互操作性：- **工具名带命名空间。** 只注册 `emergency_plan`，不占用内置工具或其他插件的裸名。
- **无服务键冲突。** 不提供任何 service key。
- **无 slot 与路由冲突。** 不注册客户端 slot，也不注册 `webServer` 前缀。
- **不监听共享事件。** 没有 `ctx.on` 订阅，因此不存在事件链被短路的问题。
- **依赖缺失时不挂载。** 只 `inject: ['tools']`；没有 `tools` 服务时不会注册工具。
- **patch 层不覆盖别人。** bundle patch 只 `insert` 自己那一行，从不覆写内置行的 `config`。
- **不改全局。** 不改原型、不改写 `process.env`、不替换全局 fetch dispatch。

dsh-emergency-plan README · dsh-emergency-plan：**Check an emergency plan's element completeness clause by clause, and locate every difference by page or line — the judgement stays with the reviewer.**

A DeepSeek Harness checker for safety managers and plan writers: it reads one plan's section tree, headings, page numbers and body text, applies a versioned rule pack for the plan type the material declares, and reports what is missing, what is empty, and where it sits.

dsh-emergency-plan README · What it is：`dsh-emergency-plan` reads one emergency plan — its section tree, headings, page numbers and body text — applies a versioned rule pack for the plan type the material declares (comprehensive, special or on-site), and checks the plan's element completeness: which elements are present, which are absent, which appear only as a heading with no body beneath, and where each one sits, by page when the material carries page numbers and by line otherwise. Every finding names the clause it came from and states whether that clause is a direct requirement, a principle or a local configuration; a check that could not run says so in `skipped` instead of passing silently. It reports literal differences between the material and the cited clauses only — no judgement on content quality, compliance, liability or safety. It runs entirely locally: no network requests, no model calls, and the source material is never modified.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Core capabilities：- **Element lists per plan type** — `EP-001` checks a special plan against 7.1–7.4, `EP-002` a comprehensive plan against 6.1–6.5, `EP-003` an on-site plan against 8.1–8.4. A heading that exists with no body text is reported as empty.
- **Page- or line-level location** — a finding carries the section's `page` when the material has one, otherwise its `line`, otherwise the heading itself. `EP-006` flags weak locating information when too few sections carry pages.
- **The rule pack is data** — element lists, aliases and thresholds live in `rules/emergency-plan.yaml`. Point `rulesFile` at another YAML to switch guideline versions or an institutional template; no code change.
- **Citations you can verify** — every rule carries a document, a number, a clause, a verbatim excerpt, a basis kind and a source URL. An excerpt shorter than eight characters, or a principle-derived check declared `error`, fails at load.
- **Nothing passes silently** — an unset element list, a disabled attachment check and an unorderable `EP-005` all land in `skipped`. The report lists differences only, and a wording guard rejects adjudicating language.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rules at a glance：| Rule | Check | Severity | Basis kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EP-001` | a special plan carries its 7.1–7.4 elements | warn | direct |
| `EP-002` | a comprehensive plan carries its 6.1–6.5 elements | warn | direct |
| `EP-003` | an on-site plan carries its 8.1–8.4 elements | warn | direct |
| `EP-004` | the material declares which of the three types it is | warn | direct |
| `EP-005` | the elements appear in the guideline's order | info | principle |
| `EP-006` | the sections carry page numbers, so a finding can be located | info | principle |
| `EP-007` | no element heading appears twice | warn | principle |
| `EP-008` | a version or revision marker is present, as configured | info | local |
| `EP-009` | the plan carries the attachment information (off by default) | info | direct |

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rules at a glance：The element lists live in the rule pack, not in the code, because they change with the guideline's version. Severities reflect that GB/T 29639 is a **recommended** national standard: an incomplete element list is a `warn`, not an `error`.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rule-by-rule answers：| You ask | What it answers |
|---|---|
| The material never says which of the three plan types it is. What happens? | `EP-004` reports the material for not declaring `planType`, because each of the three types carries a different element list. It checks only that the declaration is there, not that it is the right one; while it is missing, `EP-002` and `EP-003` state in `skipped` which element list they assumed. |
| A comprehensive plan has no later-stage handling chapter (6.4). Is that reported — and does it also need a drafting-purpose section? | `EP-002` looks for the five first-level elements of the current guideline's chapter 6 (6.1–6.5) one by one and reports each one it cannot find, so a missing later-stage handling chapter is reported. The drafting-purpose element is not one of the five: the current edition removed it, and the pack accepts it only as an alias of the general-provisions element (6.1). The finding is `warn`, because the drafting guideline is a recommended national standard, not a mandatory one. |
| Which elements are mandatory in a special plan and in an on-site plan? | `EP-001` requires the special plan's 7.1–7

dsh-emergency-plan README · Standards it follows：**Boundary:** this plugin checks an **emergency plan's element completeness** against the drafting guideline and locates each element by page, reporting literal differences against cited clauses. It is not `dsh-rulefile-check` (which audits a regulatory document's legality) and not `dsh-hidden-risk-map` (which maps a hazard ledger to determination clauses). It reads one plan and reports which elements are present, absent or empty, and where.

>
> **1. "Eight elements" is not a current requirement.** The familiar nine-name list belongs to
> **GB/T 29639—2013**, which has been **entirely replaced**; its namesake is not found in any current
> national document. The standard in force, **GB/T 29639-2020**, gives the comprehensive plan **five**
> first-level elements in clause 6 (6.1–6.5), and its foreword records that the drafting-purpose
> element was removed. Any rule citing 2013 clause numbers is citing a withdrawn standard. This pack
> cites only the 2020 clause numbers, and a test asserts that the 2013 number never appears.
>
> **2. Page numbers have no mandatory basis.** No national document requires a plan to carry page
> numbers; the appendix that governs the table of contents is an **informative appendix** (not
> normative) and does not contain the word for "page number". Page numbers are therefore treated as
> **locating information that helps a reviewer**, reported at `info`, and never phrased as "does not
> comply with X". When a plan carries no page numbers the report falls back to line numbers.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Configuration：- `EP-001` / `EP-002` / `EP-003` `elements` — the element list per plan type, as `[{ name, aliases }]`. Replace it to check against a different guideline version or your own institution's template. An empty list makes the rule report that it could not run.
- `EP-006` `minPageRatio` — the share of sections that must carry a page number before the rule stays quiet; 0.5 by default.
- `EP-008` `versionPatterns` — the strings that count as a version marker for your templates. Empty means the rule does not run.
- `EP-009` `requireAttachments` — off by default, because a caller usually supplies the body without attachments; enable it only when the attachments are actually in the material.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Material format：The tool accepts JSON or YAML, and also a plain-text plan. The section-tree form is preferred, because the caller that extracted the plan already knows where each heading sits:

```yaml
name: 某公司生产安全事故综合应急预案
planType: comprehensive         # comprehensive | special | on-site
sections:
  - { title: 总则, page: 1, body: 本预案适用于…… }

dsh-emergency-plan README · Material format：Headings are matched against each element's aliases in three widening steps: exact normalized equality, containment, then a small edit distance, so that a numbered or reworded heading still finds its element:

```text
五、保障措施              → 应急保障
二、组织机构与职责        → 应急组织机构及职责
一、总则 / 1.1 / **…**    → numbering prefixes stripped

dsh-emergency-plan README · 总则                    → markdown heading form：```

Numbering prefixes (Chinese ordinals, `1.1`, `**…**`) are stripped before comparison. Pasting markdown also works and is split on the headings, without page numbers — the report then says so. A plain-text outline works too: one short heading per line.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rule sources：Rule data lives in `rules/emergency-plan.yaml`. Every rule carries a document, a document number, a clause in the source's own numbering, a verbatim excerpt and the URL the excerpt was read from. The loader enforces that an excerpt is a real quotation of at least eight characters, and that a check resting only on a general principle or a local policy can never be declared `error`.

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rule sources：The clauses quoted come from **GB/T 29639-2020** clauses 5.1, 6, 7, 8, appendix C.1 and C.3, and from the management measure (State Administration of Work Safety Order No. 88, as amended) articles 13, 14, 15 and 16.

Three findings shaped this pack and are recorded in its header:

dsh-emergency-plan README · Rule sources：1. **"Eight elements" comes from a withdrawn standard.** The current comprehensive-plan list has five first-level elements, and the drafting-purpose element was removed.
2. **Page numbers have no mandatory basis**, so they are a locating aid at `info` level, never a non-conformity.
3. **The standard code prefix changed.** Ministry of Emergency Management Announcement No. 1 of 2025 moved AQ/T 9011-2019 and ten other standards to the **YJ** prefix, keeping number, year and content — so the companion evaluation guide is now written **YJ/T 9011-2019 (formerly AQ/T 9011-2019)**. The evaluation guide is separate from the drafting guideline: GB/T 29639 governs **drafting**, YJ/T 9011 governs **evaluation**.

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：<details>
<summary>Where does the material go? Does the plugin use the network?</summary>

No network requests, no model calls, no file writes. The material is read from `file` or inline `material`, checked in a pure function, and returned as the tool result; the plugin itself persists and uploads nothing. How the host records tool output is the host's decision.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Does an empty issue list mean the plan is compliant?</summary>

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：No. An empty issue list only means the rules that ran found no differences; every entry in `skipped` states why it did not run. All rules are capped at `warn` / `info`, the report always carries a disclaimer, and the wording guard rejects compliance, liability or correctness verdicts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Can a plan omit page numbers?</summary>

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：No national document requires page numbers. `EP-006` treats them as a locating aid: it stays quiet once the share of sections with a page reaches `minPageRatio`, and below that only raises an `info` finding. Without pages the report locates by line number and never phrases the gap as a breach of a clause.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Does it fight other plugins over names?</summary>

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：It registers exactly one tool, `emergency_plan`; no commands, no service key, no client slot, no `webServer` prefix, and no shared-event listeners. Its bundle patch only `insert`s its own row. The point-by-point argument is in "Interoperability with other DSH plugins".

</details>

<details>
<summary>How long does one check take?</summary>

dsh-emergency-plan README · FAQ：A pure function over one pass of the section tree; the pack has 9 rules, with no network or model calls. Time depends on material size and section count; the repository publishes no benchmark numbers, so none are quoted here.

</details>

dsh-emergency-plan README · Troubleshooting：- **Every element check reports itself as skipped.** The rule pack's `elements` list is empty for that plan type, or the material never declared `planType` and the check declined to assume one.
- **A heading you know exists is reported as missing.** Add it to that element's `aliases`. Matching is literal (with the three widening steps above), not semantic, by design.
- **`EP-005` reports nothing about order.** The sections carry neither `page` nor `line`, so there is nothing to order by; the rule says so in `skipped`.
- **`EP-006` complains about page numbers on a plan that has none.** That is the point of the rule, and it is `info`: it is telling you the report can only cite line numbers. Lower `minPageRatio` or read past it.
- **The plugin installs but the tool never appears.** Check that `main` resolves to `lib/index.mjs` and that `pnpm run build` produced it; a wrong `main` makes the loader skip the entry silently.
- **`dsh plugin add` refuses the package as incompatible.** The peer range covers `0.1.x` and `0.2.x`; if your runtime sits outside it, grant an explicit exemption: `dsh plugin --profile <name> allow-version dsh-emergency-p

dsh-emergency-plan README · Security boundaries & known limitations：- **Read-only and local.** The plugin reads `file` or inline `material`, writes nothing back, makes no network request and calls no model; the `package.json` demo declares `network: false` and `writes: []`.
- **No adjudication.** It lists literal differences between the material and the cited clauses; compliance, liability and content quality stay with the reviewer. The rendering layer runs a wording guard and always carries a disclaimer.
- **Severity follows the evidence.** `derived-from-principle` is capped at `warn` and `institutional-configuration` at `info`; a pack that declares a principle-derived check `error` fails at load.
- **An empty result is not a pass.** An unset element list, a disabled attachment check and an unorderable item all appear in `skipped`.
- **Page numbers are not mandatory.** See FAQ and correction 2; `EP-006` is an `info` hint only.
- **Matching is literal, not semantic.** Headings go through normalized equality, containment and edit distance; add synonym spellings to the element's `aliases`. The plugin does not judge whether the body text is any good.
- **`planType` missing or unrecogn

dsh-emergency-plan README · Interoperability with other DSH plugins：- **Namespaced tool name.** It registers only `emergency_plan`, never a bare name owned by a shipped tool or another plugin.
- **No service-key collision.** It provides no service key at all.
- **No slot or route collision.** It registers no client slot and no `webServer` prefix.
- **No shared-event listeners.** There is no `ctx.on` subscription, so no event chain can be short-circuited.
- **It does not mount without its dependency.** It declares `inject: ['tools']`; without the `tools` service the tool is not registered.
- **The patch layer overrides nothing.** The bundle patch only `insert`s its own row; it never rewrites a built-in row's `config`.
- **No global mutation.** It does not patch prototypes, rewrite `process.env`, or replace the global fetch dispatcher.
